subtopics.title: PSLV-C62 failure and its cause
subtopics.summary: ISRO's first launch of 2026, PSLV-C62, was scheduled from Sriharikota in Andhra Pradesh. A third-stage solid rocket anomaly disrupted high-thrust delivery to the upper stages, which affected the intended satellite orbital injection. The failure came 8 months after the PSLV-C61 setback.
facts: Mission was ISRO's first launch of 2026
Scheduled liftoff from Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh
Fault: 3rd-stage solid rocket anomaly
Effect: high-thrust delivery to upper stages disrupted
Impact: intended satellite orbital injection affected
Failure came 8 months after the PSLV-C61 setback

subtopics.title: PSLV rocket profile and history
subtopics.summary: The Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle is called the Workhorse of ISRO and is a four-stage medium-lift launcher, first launched in 1993. It uses solid propellants in its first and third stages and liquid propellants in its second (Vikas engine) and fourth stages. It can carry up to 1750 kg to a 600 km Sun-synchronous orbit.
facts: Nickname: Workhorse of ISRO
Type: four-stage medium-lift launch vehicle
Launched in 1993; first success in 1994 with IRS-P2
Stages 1 and 3 use solid propellants
Stages 2 (Vikas engine) and 4 use liquid propellants
First Indian launch vehicle equipped with liquid stages
Payload: up to 1750 kg to a 600 km Sun-synchronous orbit
Record: 104 satellites in one launch (2017)
Notable missions: Chandrayaan-1, Mars Orbiter Mission, Aditya-L1, AstroSat

subtopics.title: PSLV-C62 payloads
subtopics.summary: PSLV-C62 carried EOS-N1 (Anvesha), a hyperspectral imaging satellite developed for DRDO's Strategic Applications, and KID, a small re-entry prototype from a Spanish startup. It also carried AayulSAT, India's first on-orbit satellite refuelling payload. In total, 18 co-passenger satellites flew on the mission.

EOS-N1 developed for DRDO's Strategic Applications

subtopics.title: ISRO launch vehicles, private players and policy
subtopics.summary: India's launch vehicle family ranges from the early SLV and GSLV to the planned NGLV, which has a maximum payload capability of 30 tonnes. The SSLV serves small satellites and takes that load off the PSLV. Private firms such as Agnikul Cosmos are building their own rockets, which the Indian Space Policy 2023 allows.

GSLV: carries heavier satellites much deeper into space

Indian Space Policy 2023 lets private enterprises carry out end-to-end space activities
RHUMI-1: India's first reusable hybrid rocket, developed by Space Zone India

quizzes.passage: The PSLV-C62 flight carried a main satellite along with several other payloads. Among the passengers was EOS-N1, also called Anvesha, which is a satellite with an imaging instrument. A second payload, KID, was a vehicle built by a firm from abroad, and its job was to test how a small craft comes back through the atmosphere. Another payload, AayulSAT, came from a company based in Bengaluru and was among the technology demonstrations on the launch. Commercial customers from several countries also sent their satellites on the same flight, which made the list of passengers a long one. The rocket was set to lift off from Sriharikota in Andhra Pradesh. The mission followed an earlier setback in the same programme and was ISRO's first launch of the year 2026. The PSLV is a four-stage vehicle that was first launched in 1993 and uses solid propellants in its first and third stages and liquid propellants in its second and fourth stages. Its notable missions include Chandrayaan-1, the Mars Orbiter Mission and AstroSat. ISRO was formerly known as INCOSPAR and was renamed in 1969, and it is headquartered in Bengaluru. The Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System, known as NavIC, is another ISRO programme. Its payload capability is up to 1750 kg.

quizzes.passage: PSLV-C62 was a flight of the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, a rocket that ISRO calls its workhorse. The mission was planned for liftoff from Sriharikota, and it carried several payloads beyond its main satellite. One of these was EOS-N1, an imaging satellite that supports observation of the Earth from space. Another passenger was KID, a small prototype designed to return from space. KID was built by a startup from abroad. AayulSAT, a payload from a Bengaluru company, is a technology test linked to satellites that are already in orbit. Commercial customers from several countries also flew satellites on the mission. The PSLV is a medium-lift vehicle with a payload capability of up to 1750 kg, and its notable missions include Chandrayaan-1, the Mars Orbiter Mission and AstroSat. The Mars Orbiter Mission was the first Asian spacecraft to enter Martian orbit. ISRO is India's national space agency, and its headquarters are in Bengaluru. ISRO was formerly known as INCOSPAR and was renamed in 1969. The Indian Space Policy 2023 is the government's plan to let private enterprises carry out end-to-end activities. The Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System, known as NavIC, is another ISRO programme. The flight was ISRO's first launch in 2026, following a setback in the previous mission.

quizzes.passage: India's launch vehicles come in several families, and each has its own role. Early rockets in the line came first, and newer designs followed. The Next Generation Launch Vehicle is a planned rocket, still in development, that is meant to carry much larger payloads than the current options. The NGLV is designed to be reusable and green. It is expected to enable missions such as human spaceflight. Another rocket, the Small Satellite Launch Vehicle, has flown test missions and is launched from Sriharikota. The SSLV is a three-stage vehicle, and its producing body is NSIL. Private companies have also started building rockets of their own. Agnikul Cosmos is one such company, and its rockets are launched from a privately developed launchpad. Its founders include Srinath Ravichandran, Moin SPM and Satya Chakravarthy, and its rocket is described as the world's first with a fully 3D-printed engine. The Indian Space Policy is the government's plan to let private enterprises take part in space activity. The Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre, based in Ahmedabad, helps private players take part in space activity. ISRO, India's national space agency, is headquartered in Bengaluru. The Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle, GSLV, has a Mk-III version that made ISRO entirely self-sufficient.

quizzes.passage: ISRO's rockets fall into different families, and each has its own role. The SLV was ISRO's first satellite launch vehicle, and the ASLV followed it. The GSLV has a Mk-III version that made ISRO self-sufficient, and it is meant to carry heavier satellites deeper into space. The SSLV is one of the smaller members of that family, and its test flights have shown what it can do. The SSLV is a three-stage vehicle, and its launch site is Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota. The SSLV is produced by NSIL. The NGLV is a much larger rocket that is still being planned, with a big payload target, and it is designed to be reusable and green. On the private side, Agnikul Cosmos works on launch systems and uses a launchpad of its own. Agnikul Cosmos was founded by three people, including Srinath Ravichandran, and its engine is described as the world's first fully 3D-printed one. Another private effort is a rocket of a different design that was launched with a partner group and carried a few small satellites. The Indian Space Policy is the government's plan that opens space activity to private firms. ISRO is India's national space agency, and its headquarters are in Bengaluru.
